headline: High: AutoGen’s writable, broad-egress execution environment can feed sensitive support data into cognee’s memory workflows, creating leakage and cascading-error risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write the filesystem and execute shell/subprocesses, while cognee ingests documents and workflows via CLI/API surfaces. If AutoGen writes attacker-controlled content into a shared workspace, cognee may treat it as trusted input. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation between them, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF cognee ingests files produced by AutoGen without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Add a manual review step before cognee ingests AutoGen output
Tag AutoGen outputs with provenance metadata
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys; cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history. If they share a workspace or session data, AutoGen can transmit sensitive material to external model providers, while cognee’s memory-oriented workflows can retain it. That creates a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive data in both profiles.
conditions: IF AutoGen receives files or prompts containing support, finance, or personal data
IF cognee stores the same data class in its memory/workflow layer
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of AutoGen prompts
Route only redacted excerpts into cognee
Rotate and scope API keys used by AutoGen
Separate tenant/workspace storage between agents
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; cognee is CLI-driven and may also mutate local state, but its write scope is not documented here. Because both can operate on shared local resources, a write conflict is plausible, yet the exact overlap is uncertain. Per rubric, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same working directory
IF cognee writes indexes or state files in that directory
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Run only one writer at a time
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Snapshot state before each run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that produces tool outputs and code-execution results; cognee is a memory/workflow system that can consume documents and decisions. If cognee treats AutoGen output as authoritative, errors can cascade into stored knowledge or downstream workflows. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF cognee ingests AutoGen-generated facts without verification
IF downstream workflows act on cognee-stored outputs
mitigations: Require human review before ingestion
Store source citations alongside every imported fact
Reject uncited or low-confidence AutoGen outputs
Limit AutoGen to draft-only generation
requires-engineering: add verification and rollback workflows

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while AutoGen can handle model-provider API keys and broad egress. If EU or regulated customer data flows through AutoGen to external providers without a documented DPA/residency control, the pair can create a compliance breach. The profiles do not show matching residency or retention controls, so uncertainty increases severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is processed by both agents
IF AutoGen sends that data to third-party model providers without a DPA or residency control
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from AutoGen prompts
Use a compliant provider configuration
Document retention and deletion handling
Restrict cognee to non-regulated datasets
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
